why:
I checked each of the verifier's four PASS/FAIL pairs against its expect line, and the criterion holds for all of them.

- **Check 1** tests only what the words require: that padLeft is exported, pads on the left with the given fill, falls back to a space when no fill is given, and reaches width characters ("xx7", "00042", "  ab").
- **Check 2** tests only that inputs of equal length and longer come back unchanged.
- **Check 3** requires each exported function to have "its own section… a heading that names the function, with text under it." That is a fair reading of "section", not a stricter test, and it leaves heading style open. Naming padLeft follows from line 1.
- **Check 4** requires only that npm test passes.

The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)": whether padLeft tests were added, how a multi-character fill behaves, whether headings match the `## name(args)` style, and whether the README mentions the default fill.
